concept.name: Purged cross-validation
concept.definition: A time-series cross-validation design that removes training observations whose label-information intervals overlap a test fold.
concept.intuition: It estimates how a fitted choice behaves on observations that were not used to fit that choice.
concept.mechanics: Represent each sample by its information start and label end, create a test fold, then purge any training interval that intersects the test intervals.
concept.failure_modes: Random splitting, overlapping labels, repeated tuning, or an unprotected final test set can produce optimistic estimates.
concept.misconceptions: Validation measures conditional generalization under a split design; it does not guarantee future market performance.
concept.example: If a Friday label uses returns through Wednesday, training rows whose labels also use that Monday-Wednesday interval are removed when Friday is tested.

citations.source: A Bayesian-based classification framework for financial time series trend prediction
